podcast.title: Captain Biscuit

hosts.Leyla: lives in Baku and loves a good plan
hosts.Sam: grew up in Manchester and once travelled with no plan at all

before.predict: Do you have a scar with a story? Guess: who was Sam's best friend when he was little?

lines.t: Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is childhood memories. So let's take a trip down memory lane.
[laugh] OK! Do you see this little scar on my knee?
Yes. What happened?
I was seven. I was riding my brother's bike in our courtyard, much too fast, and I crashed into the grandmothers' bench.
Oh no! Were the grandmothers OK?
They were fine. I was crying, and all of them were shouting at the same time. I remember it like it was yesterday.
[chuckle] My strongest memory is my imaginary friend. His name was Captain Biscuit.
Captain Biscuit?
He was a pirate, and he lived under my bed. When I broke something, it was always Captain Biscuit's fault.
[laugh] Clever boy. Did your parents believe you?
Never. My mum was quite strict. She said, "Then Captain Biscuit can tidy your room."
My parents were strict about homework, but our school was even stricter. Our maths teacher never smiled. Not once in four years.
What did you do at break time?
We ran to the playground and played hide and seek, or jumped rope for hours. No phones, just friends.
Same for me. We played football until it was dark, and then our mums called us in for dinner.
Children grow up so differently now. My niece Aysu plays games on a tablet.
But she also does science experiments at the kitchen table!
True. Maybe it's not so different. Kids still want adventures.
And imaginary friends. I'm sure Captain Biscuit is still under some little boy's bed.
[laugh] Here's your question for your next SpeakLab call: what is your happiest childhood memory — and why do you still remember it?
Mine is every time Captain Biscuit got the blame. See you next time!
Bye for now!
